citation: A committee of five representing the Association of Teachers of Psychology in Iowa. (1911). Preparation for Examinations in Psychology. The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/edu
title: Recommended list of ten psychology textbooks with Elementary and Advanced requirements
description: To secure a uniform basis for the examinations, the committee recommends ten texts, including Betts, Angell, Kirkpatrick, James, Seashore, Judd, Dewey, Titchener, Calkins, and Thorndike, each annotated (e.g., Seashore's is "A manual of experiments not requiring any laboratory"). The article states "In the Elementary examination, three of these are required; in the Advanced, six." Special books are Kirkpatrick, Seashore, and Dewey; the others are general introductions. A supplementary reference list for public libraries is also given.
requirements: Candidates select two general and one special text for the Elementary examination, four general and two special for the Advanced
constraints: The state examination will be based specifically upon the recommended books only until January 1, 1915, with a revision published January 1, 1914
target_learners: Teachers seeking Elementary or Advanced psychology certification in Iowa
target_learning_goals: Preparation for uniform state psychology examinations
key_sources: A committee of five representing the Association of Teachers of Psychology in Iowa. (1911). Preparation for Examinations in Psychology. The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/edu

citation: Vania Dimitrova. (2003). STyLE-OLM: Interactive Open Learner Modelling. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://telearn.hal.science/hal-00197312
title: Adaptive learning systems should diagnose learners through interactive open learner modelling
description: Because diagnosing a learner's cognitive capacity is crucial for adaptive systems, the article recommends conceiving diagnosis as an interactive process: systems should let the learner discuss and jointly construct the learner model. The authors argue IOLM "is a fruitful approach which may be employed in intelligent learning environments".
requirements: An intelligent learning environment that opens the learner model to inspection and negotiation with the learner
target_learners: learners using adaptive computer-based learning systems
target_learning_goals: improved diagnosis of the learner's cognitive state
examples: STyLE-OLM implements this approach by having the system and learner discuss and together construct the learner model
key_sources: Vania Dimitrova. (2003). STyLE-OLM: Interactive Open Learner Modelling. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://telearn.hal.science/hal-00197312
